prompt.context: Our client, Multinational Refrigerated Food Company (RFC), is contemplating the introduction of a refrigerated pizza product to the US market. Several years ago, RFC entered the refrigerated food market introducing the Pasta and toppings concept, which was very successful earning sales over $200M in two years. Now the marketing management of RFC plans to extend its product line into pizza, and has hired McKinsey to help them assess the new market opportunity and advise whether they should launch or not the new product.
prompt.question: What factors should we investigate to determine whether RFC should expand its brand into a new product line, and should they launch the refrigerated pizza product?

clarifying_info.q: What is management's definition of a successful product launch?
clarifying_info.a: Management's KPI for a successful product launch is $80M in revenues in the first year of sales.

clarifying_info.q: Are there any competitors in the refrigerated pizza space?
clarifying_info.a: There are no competitors within the refrigerated pizza concept.

clarifying_info.q: Who are the competitors in the broader pizza market?
clarifying_info.a: Overall the pizza market is dominated by delivery/takeout chains and restaurants.

clarifying_info.q: What product concepts is management considering?
clarifying_info.a: Management is looking to choose between two concepts: a pizza 'kit' where toppings for pizza are sold separately, and a pre-assembled heat-and-eat pizza.

exhibits.title: Marketing Department Information
exhibits.shows: A two-part table from the marketing department. Part A shows Awareness and ACV data for both pizza concepts broken down by RFC Users and Non-users. Part B shows marketing survey purchase intent results ('Definitely would buy', 'Probably would buy', 'Top two boxes') for both concepts broken down by RFC Users and Non-users, with an industry average column.

exhibits.title: Perceptual Map of Pizza Only Concept
exhibits.shows: A perceptual map with two axes: Convenience (x-axis) and Quality (y-axis). Circle area represents price. Three competitors are plotted: Restaurant/Delivery pizza, Frozen pizza, and RFC's pizza concept.

framework: Understanding the market and its size: major players including customers, competitors, and suppliers
Estimating the financial aspects of entry: projected revenues tested against the $80M KPI
Understanding RFC's capabilities to execute the move into the new segment
Outlining major risks for RFC with this product line extension
Evaluating the two product concepts (pizza kit vs. heat-and-eat) and which to pursue
Assessing first-mover advantage given absence of direct refrigerated pizza competition
Considering brand awareness spillover from existing RFC pasta concept user base

questions.prompt: What factors should RFC investigate to determine whether to expand its brand into a new pizza product line?
questions.guidance: A strong framework covers: (1) Market size and structure — customers, competitors, suppliers; (2) Financial feasibility — project revenues vs. $80M KPI; (3) Company capabilities — supply chain, distribution, manufacturing; (4) Risks — brand dilution, execution risk. A great candidate also notes the two product concept options, the first-mover advantage from having no refrigerated pizza competitors, and that existing pasta-concept users may have higher brand awareness and purchase propensity for the new line.

questions.prompt: Without making any calculations, what insights can you draw from Exhibit 1 (the marketing survey)?
questions.guidance: A good answer covers: (1) RFC Users and Non-users show materially different purchase intents — the user/non-user split will significantly influence sales estimates; (2) Neither concept hits the industry average top-two-box score for Non-users (Pizza & Toppings = 40%, Pizza Only = 80% vs. industry 61% — Pizza Only exceeds industry for Non-users but Pizza & Toppings does not), indicating caution for one concept; (3) A decision cannot be made confidently from this exhibit alone. A great answer also notes: the exhibit enables trial volume calculations if retail price and targeted population are known; the large spread between 'definitely' and 'probably' for Non-users warrants follow-up; stated purchase intent overstates actual purchase behavior, so adjustment factors are needed.

questions.prompt: Calculate the first-year sales for both pizza concepts. Given: targeted households = 120M, RFC penetration rate = 50%, pizza price = $7/pizza (Pizza Only), pizza and toppings price = $5/pizza (Pizza & Toppings), conversion: 'definitely would buy' → 70% actually buy, 'probably would buy' → 20% actually buy, average units purchased per trial = 2.
questions.guidance: A good candidate identifies that missing information needed includes targeted population split by RFC users vs. non-users, price for both concepts, and conversion rates. A great candidate also flags that total sales = trial sales + repeat sales, so repeat rate is also required — interviewers should give positive feedback for this but tell the candidate to ignore repeat sales for simplicity. Candidates should be very structured: compute RFC Users sales and Non-users sales separately for each concept, then sum. The conclusion is that Pizza Only (~$119M) exceeds the $80M KPI while Pizza & Toppings (~$81M) barely meets it — management should proceed with the Pizza Only concept.

math.setup: Total Sales = RFC Users sales + Non-users sales, for each concept. Formula per group: (Targeted HH) x (RFC penetration or non-penetration rate) x Awareness x ACV x (Def_buy% x 70% + Prob_buy% x 20%) x Avg units x Price
steps: RFC Users base = 120M x 50% = 60M households; Non-users base = 120M x 50% = 60M households
Pizza & Toppings — RFC Users: 60M x 60% awareness x 60% ACV x (30%x70% + 60%x20%) x 2 x $5 = 60M x 0.60 x 0.60 x (0.21+0.12) x 2 x 5 = 60M x 0.36 x 0.33 x 10 = 71.28M
Pizza & Toppings — Non-users: 60M x 20% awareness x 60% ACV x (10%x70% + 30%x20%) x 2 x $5 = 60M x 0.20 x 0.60 x (0.07+0.06) x 2 x 5 = 60M x 0.12 x 0.13 x 10 = 9.36M
math.answer: Pizza & Toppings: ~$80.64M (barely meets $80M KPI). Pizza Only: ~$118.69M (well exceeds $80M KPI). Recommend Pizza Only concept.

questions.prompt: (Bonus) The management decided to study the Pizza Only concept further. What insights can you draw from the perceptual map in Exhibit 2?
questions.guidance: The candidate should identify that RFC's pizza concept faces a positioning risk: its quality is not high enough to compete with Restaurant/Delivery pizza, yet its price makes it difficult to compete on price with Frozen pizza. RFC's product sits in an unfavorable middle ground. The client should focus on improving convenience (faster cooking time, easier preparation) to attract customers from the Restaurant/Delivery segment, since competing on price versus frozen pizza is difficult given the need for fresh dough and ingredients.

recommendation: RFC should launch the pizza concept and pursue the Pizza Only (heat-and-eat) concept
The Pizza Only concept is projected to generate ~$118.69M in first-year sales, well above the $80M KPI — almost $38M more than the Pizza & Toppings concept
The success of the existing Pasta concept has created a loyal customer base with 60% awareness among RFC users, providing a stable foundation for the new product launch
risks: The marketing survey may overstate actual purchase intent; repeat purchase rate has not been factored into projections
Perceptual map shows RFC's pizza is not well-positioned against the Restaurant/Delivery segment on quality, limiting upside with that consumer group
Competing on price with the Frozen pizza segment is difficult given the need for fresh dough and refrigerated ingredients
next_steps: Verify accuracy and completeness of the marketing survey data
Incorporate repeat purchase rate into a more detailed sales model
Develop a positioning and marketing strategy to improve perceived convenience and quality relative to the Restaurant/Delivery segment
Come back to management with more detailed recommendations including go-to-market plan
